exposure: Primiparous women with term, singleton, cephalic, vaginal delivery
cohort: Primiparous women with term, singleton, cephalic, vaginal delivery from a national database between 2008 and 2014
finding: Episiotomy may be a risk or protective factor for obstetric anal sphincter injuries depending on the type of episiotomy and the clinical setting in which it is used.
mod_finding: Mediolateral episiotomy increased the risk for obstetric anal sphincter injuries in spontaneous vaginal birth, whereas it was protective in vacuum delivery.
